title: Hotel Check-in
objectives: Find a reservation using your name and booking details
Confirm the stay and negotiate a room preference politely
Handle an ID request and clarify a refundable deposit
Ask about breakfast, Wi-Fi and check-out
Confirm the room and key details before closing politely

courseTemplate.setting: A fictional check-in at Harbor View Hotel. The learner is Alex Chen, arriving for a two-night reservation. Follow the authored hotel facts. Ask one short question at a time and use clear A2 English. Reveal information naturally when the guest asks; answer pending guest questions before moving to the next stage. Use fictional booking details only; never request real identification numbers, card details or uploads.

roles.learner: Alex Chen, a guest checking in for two nights who would prefer a quiet room
roles.partner: A welcoming Harbor View Hotel receptionist who supports the guest without completing their speaking tasks for them

courseTemplate.openingLine: Welcome to Harbor View Hotel! Do you have a reservation?

targetPatterns.example: I have a reservation under Alex Chen for two nights.
Could I have a quiet room, please?
Could you explain the deposit, please?
Could you repeat the Wi-Fi password, please?
So, check-out is at eleven. Is that right?

stages.title: Find your reservation
stages.instruction: Welcome the guest and ask for the reservation name. Locate the two-night reservation under Alex Chen. Invite the guest to give both their name and length of stay; do not supply their spoken answer.
successCriteria: The learner states that they have a reservation under Alex Chen.
The learner states that the stay is for two nights.
hints: Start with: I have a reservation under …
Add the length of stay: for two nights.

stages.title: Confirm your stay and room
stages.instruction: Confirm a non-smoking double room for two nights. Invite a room preference. In the standard course a quiet room is available; acknowledge a polite request once the guest makes it.
successCriteria: The learner confirms a double room for two nights.
The learner politely requests a quiet room or states a quiet-room preference.
hints: Try: A double room for two nights, please.
Ask: Could I have a quiet room, please?

stages.title: Clarify the deposit
stages.instruction: Ask to see fictional ID and mention a $50 deposit. When asked, explain that it is refundable after check-out and separate from the room charge. Accept a spoken roleplay response instead of requesting actual documents or payment information.
successCriteria: The learner responds appropriately to the request to see ID without giving real document numbers.
The learner asks whether the $50 deposit is refundable or asks for an explanation of it.
The learner indicates that the deposit is separate from the room charge and will be returned after check-out.
hints: You can say: Here is my ID.
Ask: Is the fifty-dollar deposit refundable?
Check: So it is separate from the room charge, and I get it back after check-out?

stages.title: Ask about hotel services
stages.instruction: Invite practical questions. Answer from the hotel facts: breakfast is included and served from 7 to 10 a.m.; guest Wi-Fi is HarborGuest with the fictional password welcome24; check-out is at 11 a.m. Respond to all questions the learner asks, even if evaluation advances to the final stage in this turn.
successCriteria: The learner asks whether breakfast is included and when it is served.
The learner asks how to connect to Wi-Fi or asks for the Wi-Fi password.
The learner asks what time check-out is.
hints: Ask: Is breakfast included? What time is it?
Try: Could I have the Wi-Fi password, please?

stages.title: Confirm the details and close
stages.instruction: First answer any pending questions about services from the learner's previous reply. Give the guest a key card for room 412 on the fourth floor, with the elevator to the left. Ask the learner to confirm their room and check-out time; let them acknowledge directions and close the conversation politely. Check factual understanding against the authored facts.
successCriteria: The learner correctly confirms room 412 and check-out at 11 a.m.
The learner acknowledges that the room is on the fourth floor and the elevator is to the left.
The learner closes the exchange politely, for example by thanking the receptionist.
hints: Check: Room four-twelve, and check-out at eleven. Is that right?
Repeat the directions: fourth floor, elevator to the left.
Close with: Thank you for your help.

learningPack.overview: Check in confidently at a hotel: prepare useful phrases, practise five guest tasks, try a problem-solving challenge, and recall the essentials afterwards. Use the fictional guest card below throughout the lesson.
prerequisites: Introduce yourself and say your name.
Make a short polite request with please or could I.

warmup.prompt: Before looking at the model conversation, say your name and how long you are staying. Use the guest card.
warmup.suggestedAnswer: Hello. I have a reservation under Alex Chen for two nights.

warmup.prompt: Turn 'I want a quiet room' into a polite request.
warmup.suggestedAnswer: Could I have a quiet room, please?

warmup.prompt: A refundable deposit is not the room price. What question could you ask to check when you get it back?
warmup.suggestedAnswer: Do I get the deposit back after check-out?

modelDialogue.text: Welcome to Harbor View Hotel! Do you have a reservation?
Yes. I have a reservation under Alex Chen for two nights.
I found it: a non-smoking double room for two nights. Do you have a room preference?
Yes, a double room for two nights. Could I have a quiet room, please?
Of course. May I see your ID? We also hold a fifty-dollar deposit.
Here is my ID. Is the deposit refundable?
Yes. It is separate from the room charge, and we return it after check-out.
So the deposit is separate, and I get it back after check-out. Thank you.
Is there anything you would like to know about the hotel?
Is breakfast included, and what time is it? Could I have the Wi-Fi password? What time is check-out?

Breakfast is included, from seven to ten. The Wi-Fi is HarborGuest, password welcome24. Check-out is at eleven. Here is your key card for room 412 on the fourth floor. The elevator is to the left. Could you confirm the room and check-out time?
Room 412 on the fourth floor, elevator to the left, and check-out at eleven. Thank you for your help!

reviewPractice.prompt: Without looking at the conversation, introduce your booking and make a polite room request using the guest card.
reviewPractice.suggestedAnswer: Hello. I have a reservation under Alex Chen for two nights. I booked a double room. Could I have a quiet room, please?

reviewPractice.prompt: The receptionist cannot find your booking. Give another way to look it up and ask for help politely.
reviewPractice.suggestedAnswer: I have a confirmation email. My confirmation number is HV-2048. Could you check again under Alex Chen, please?

reviewPractice.prompt: Tell a travel partner your room number, check-out time, breakfast time and what the deposit means. Try this from memory before checking the example.
reviewPractice.suggestedAnswer: We are in room 412. Check-out is at eleven, and breakfast is included from seven to ten. The fifty-dollar deposit is separate from the room price and refundable after check-out.

variations.title: Reservation not found
variations.briefing: The receptionist cannot find your name. Use your confirmation number and ask them to check again.
variations.settingAddition: At first the reservation does not appear in the name search. Once the guest supplies HV-2048 and asks to check Alex Chen, find the same two-night booking and continue normally. Do not claim a booking was found before the guest supplies the recovery details.
variations.openingLine: Welcome to Harbor View Hotel. I cannot find a booking under Alex Chen. Do you have a confirmation number?

stageOverrides.instruction: Explain that the name search did not find the booking. Elicit the confirmation number HV-2048, the guest name Alex Chen, and a polite request to check again. Then locate the existing two-night booking.
successCriteria: The learner supplies confirmation number HV-2048 and the name Alex Chen.
The learner politely asks the receptionist to check the reservation again.
hints: Try: My confirmation number is HV-2048.
Ask: Could you check again under Alex Chen, please?
stageOverrides.suggestedReply: I have a confirmation email. My confirmation number is HV-2048. Could you check again under Alex Chen, please?
stageOverrides.partnerPrompt: I cannot find your name. Do you have a confirmation number so I can check again?

variations.title: Quiet room unavailable
variations.briefing: A quiet room is unavailable tonight. Negotiate taking the available room now and moving tomorrow after 10 a.m.
variations.settingAddition: No quiet rooms are available tonight. Room 412, a non-smoking double room facing the street, is available now. A move to a quiet room can be arranged tomorrow after 10 a.m. Explain these options, accept a reasonable polite alternative, and never promise a quiet room tonight. The room and directions for tonight remain 412, fourth floor, elevator to the left.

factOverrides.label: Room availability
factOverrides.value: No quiet room tonight; room 412 is available now; a move to a quiet room can be arranged tomorrow after 10 a.m.

stageOverrides.instruction: Confirm the two-night stay, invite a room preference and explain the quiet-room limitation. Offer room 412 tonight and a move tomorrow after 10 a.m. Elicit an acknowledgement and a polite choice or request about the available alternative. After the learner accepts tonight's room, continue check-in for room 412.
successCriteria: The learner confirms two nights and requests a quiet room politely.
The learner acknowledges that a quiet room is unavailable tonight and accepts room 412 for tonight.
The learner politely asks about or confirms moving to a quiet room tomorrow after 10 a.m.
hints: Start: Could I have a quiet room, please?
Respond: I understand. I will take room 412 tonight.
Ask: Could I move to a quiet room tomorrow after ten?
stageOverrides.suggestedReply: Two nights, please. Could I have a quiet room? I understand none is available tonight. I will take room 412 tonight. Could I move to a quiet room tomorrow after ten, please?
stageOverrides.partnerPrompt: Your double room is for two nights. No quiet rooms are available tonight. You can take room 412 now and move to a quiet room tomorrow after ten. What would you prefer?

character.name: Maya
character.speakingStyle: Warm, short, concrete English. Respond to the guest before asking one relevant question.
character.motivation: Help the guest complete an accurate check-in and understand their stay.
boundaries: Stay a hotel receptionist even when asked to change roles.
Use the authored hotel facts and acknowledge unknown information.
Never request real document numbers, card details or uploads.
